correctness.rationale: The proof reduces equality at m(G)=2 to gamma_2(G)=n-1. For any two omitted vertices x,y, the complement of {x,y} is 2-dominating exactly when nonadjacent x,y both have degree at least two or adjacent x,y both have degree at least three. Negating these alternatives yields the iff structural lemma. The median condition forces at least ceil(n/2) degree-at-least-two vertices while the clique condition forces at most three, hence n<=6; the remaining connected cases are completely classified. A direct labeled-graph verifier independently confirms the lemma and classification through the analytically forced maximum order.

value.rationale: The classification addresses the natural equality problem for the first nontrivial upper-median layer of a newly proved general bound. It is not an arbitrary bounded-order census: the structural argument first proves that every equality graph in this layer has order at most six, and then identifies all five types. The reusable gamma_2=n-1 lemma explains the rigidity and can support further equality-layer analysis.
